title: Prism for coends of simplicial functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a cocomplete category, in universes containing all displayed functor categories and colimits. Use simplicial sets and standard simplices of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and combinatorial simplicial homotopies with the face and degeneracy identities of [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism]. Let $T,U:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathrm{sSet},\mathcal C)$ be simplicial diagrams of functors preserving all small colimits. For any simplicial set $K$ put
$$R_T(K)=\int^{[p]\in\Delta}T_p(K\times\Delta^p),\qquad R_U(K)=\int^{[p]\in\Delta}U_p(K\times\Delta^p),$$
where the coends are coproducts modulo the relations induced by simplex operators in $T,U$ and in the standard simplex. Let $f,g:T\to U$ be maps of simplicial diagrams and let $H_a^p:T_p\to U_{p+1}$ be natural transformations forming a combinatorial simplicial homotopy from $f$ to $g$. Then there is a map
$$\widetilde H_K:R_T(K\times\Delta^1)\longrightarrow R_U(K)$$
natural in $K$, whose restrictions along $K\times\{0\}$ and $K\times\{1\}$ are $R_f(K)$ and $R_g(K)$, respectively, after interchanging the endpoints if the homotopy is given in the opposite orientation. The map is compatible with precomposition and postcomposition of the homotopy by maps of simplicial diagrams. No splitting, enrichment or model structure is assumed.

source.place: Section 3.10, Definition 3.11 and Proposition 3.12, printed pp.12-13: contraction on realization. The proof of Proposition 3.12 is omitted, and its promised Appendix A contains only a placeholder in this version. The general prism triangulation is therefore a separate agent-stated categorical lemma, not a quoted proof. Agent categorical extension to diagrams of colimit-preserving functors, not a literal assertion of the source. Source read in the sandbox; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: For each simplicial set K, let q^T_{p,K}:T_p(K\times\Delta^p)\to R_T(K) and q^U_{p,K}:U_p(K\times\Delta^p)\to R_U(K) be the canonical coend maps. Their compatibility with every simplex operator is exactly the relation in the displayed coend definition. Applying f or g on each summand therefore gives well-defined maps R_f(K),R_g(K), and all these maps are natural in K. We use the universal property of the colimits and coproducts in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] to treat these canonical maps as unique maps out of the corresponding coends.

source.place: Stacks Categories, definition of colimit (tag 002F), applied to the coend coproduct/coequalizer

proof.text: Fix p. Interchanging the factors in the explicit maps \sigma_j of [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary] gives \kappa_j:\Delta^{p+1}\to\Delta^p\times\Delta^1 (0\le j\le p) with vertex list (0,0),\ldots,(j,0),(j,1),\ldots,(p,1). Each \kappa_j is injective on vertices into the nerve of the poset [p]\times[1], hence a monomorphism; write P_j for its image. The P_j cover \Delta^p\times\Delta^1: an n-simplex of the product is a monotone chain in [p]\times[1], and it lies in P_j for any j between the last first coordinate carrying second coordinate 0 and the first first coordinate carrying second coordinate 1 (take j=p, resp. j=0, for a chain entirely at height 0, resp. 1). For a<b, P_a\cap P_b is the face on the common vertices (0,0),\ldots,(a,0),(b,1),\ldots,(p,1), which lies in P_c for every a\le c\le b. Degreewise a union of subsets is the coequalizer of the coproduct of the pairwise intersections into the coproduct of the pieces, and colimits and products of simplicial sets are degreewise ([def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]); hence K\times(\Delta^p\times\Delta^1) is the colimit of the diagram of the K\times P_a and K\times(P_a\cap P_b), and, because T_p preserves all small colimits, so is T_p(K\times\Delta^p\times\Delta^1) for the diagram of the T_p(K\times P_a), T_p(K\times(P_a\cap P_b)). Via \kappa_j, define on the j-th piece g_j=q^U_{p+1,K}\circ H_j^p(K\times\Delta^{p+1}):T_p(K\times\Delta^{p+1})\to R_U(K).

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.12, explicit prism maps and horn filtration; factor interchange is the symmetry of the product

proof.text: Adjacent pieces P_j,P_{j+1} meet in the face omitting position j+1 in both vertex lists: \kappa_j\delta_{j+1}=\kappa_{j+1}\delta_{j+1}. By naturality of H and the U-coend relation q^U_{p+1,K}\circ U_{p+1}(K\times\delta_{j+1})=q^U_{p,K}\circ d_{j+1}, the restrictions of g_j and g_{j+1} to this face are q^U_{p,K}\circ d_{j+1}H_j^p and q^U_{p,K}\circ d_{j+1}H_{j+1}^p (evaluated at K\times\Delta^p), which agree by the middle identity d_{j+1}H_{j+1}^p=d_{j+1}H_j^p of [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism] (j<p). For a<b the intersection P_a\cap P_b lies in each of P_a\cap P_{a+1},\ldots,P_{b-1}\cap P_b, so restricting the successive adjacent agreements gives agreement of g_a and g_b on it. All pairwise restrictions therefore agree, and the colimit universal property of Step 2 glues the g_j to a unique map F_{p,K}:T_p(K\times\Delta^p\times\Delta^1)\to R_U(K); uniqueness and naturality of H, q and T_p make it natural in K. No map on the boundary \Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^p is needed at this stage; the faces lying there are compared with level p-1 in Step 4.

source.place: Section 3.10, Definition 3.11 and Proposition 3.12; the omitted proof is supplied by the explicit horn gluing above

proof.text: The maps F_{p,K} respect the coend relations in the T-variable. It is enough to check a coface and a codegeneracy, since every map in the simplex category factors as a surjection followed by an injection, hence is a composite of these. Since T_p preserves the colimit of Step 2 for \Delta^{p'}\times\Delta^1, two maps out of T_p(K\times\Delta^{p'}\times\Delta^1) agree when they agree on every piece. By the vertex lists: for a coface \delta_i:[p-1]\to[p] and 0\le j\le p-1, (\delta_i\times1)\kappa_j=\kappa_{j+1}\delta_i if i\le j and =\kappa_j\delta_{i+1} if i>j; for a codegeneracy \sigma_i:[p+1]\to[p] and 0\le j\le p+1, (\sigma_i\times1)\kappa_j=\kappa_{j-1}\sigma_i if i<j and =\kappa_j\sigma_{i+1} if i\ge j. Using naturality of H and the U-coend relations, the required equalities on the j-th piece become respectively d_iH_{j+1}^p=H_j^{p-1}d_i (i\le j) or d_{i+1}H_j^p=H_j^{p-1}d_i (i>j) for cofaces, and s_iH_{j-1}^p=H_j^{p+1}s_i (i<j) or s_{i+1}H_j^p=H_j^{p+1}s_i (i\ge j) for codegeneracies; these are exactly the two strict-inequality face identities and the two degeneracy identities of [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism]. Hence the family (F_{p,K}) descends uniquely through the coend to a map \widetilde H_K:R_T(K\times\Delta^1)\to R_U(K).

source.place: Lines 48-67, the face and degeneracy identities for combinatorial simplicial homotopy

proof.text: On the endpoint K\times\{0\}, the last face of the prism simplex κ_p gives q^U_{p+1,K}(d_{p+1}H_p^p\otimes1)=q^U_{p,K}(f_p\otimes1), using d_{p+1}H_p^p=f_p. On K\times\{1\}, the first face of κ_0 gives q^U_{p+1,K}(d_0H_0^p\otimes1)=q^U_{p,K}(g_p\otimes1), using d_0H_0^p=g_p. These identities hold on every summand and therefore, by the coend quotient, are exactly \widetilde H_K|_{K\times\{0\}}=R_f(K) and \widetilde H_K|_{K\times\{1\}}=R_g(K). Reversing the interval exchanges the endpoints.

source.place: Lines 55-56, endpoint identities; endpoint faces of the prism maps

proof.text: For a map K\to K' of simplicial sets, every construction above is obtained by applying the corresponding functorial map to K\times(-); naturality of H, f and g makes the maps on every prism piece commute, and uniqueness of the colimit gluings and coend descents gives naturality of \widetilde H. If the homotopy is precomposed by a map of T-diagrams or postcomposed by a map of U-diagrams, the same componentwise calculation replaces each g_j by its composite. Thus the glued map and its endpoint restrictions are compatible with both precomposition and postcomposition.
